items.name: IFI (Instituição Fiscal Independente, Federal Senate)
items.note: Report pages on www12.senado.leg.br sit behind a browser security check; the PDFs in the Senate digital library (www2.senado.leg.br) are open.
items.title: Relatório de Acompanhamento Fiscal – Out/2026
items.summary: The IFI expects a primary deficit of 0.5% of GDP in 2026 and a potential deficit of 1.0% of GDP in 2027, arguing that new spending commitments and lost revenue (about R$ 40 billion unbudgeted) call for a fiscal adjustment of roughly 3 percentage points of GDP. It also warns that the primary-result target misses large off-budget credit and fund operations, and that a higher neutral interest rate would raise the required primary surplus.

key_number.what: Potential primary deficit for 2027 as a percentage of GDP, which the IFI says could arise given new commitments and its differences from the PLOA 2027 figures

items.name: HCFP (Haut Conseil des finances publiques)
items.title: Avis n°2026 – 5 Lois de finances 2027
items.summary: The High Council of Public Finances judges the government's 2026 deficit forecast of 5.4% of GDP plausible, but considers the 2027 growth forecast of 1.0% optimistic and says risks to growth are mainly downward. It warns that the expected 2027 deficit reduction is too slow, that the debt-to-GDP ratio keeps rising toward about 122%, and that the 2029 target of a deficit below 3% of GDP is very unlikely to be met.

key_number.what: Expected public debt-to-GDP ratio, which the High Council says is approaching this level as debt keeps rising

items.name: Cour des comptes
items.note: Annual report on the situation and outlook of the public finances (published 25 June 2026).

items.name: México Evalúa
items.title: El reto del Paquete Económico 2027: recuperar el margen para invertir en desarrollo
items.summary: México Evalúa finds that the 2027 Economic Package would lower the broad public deficit (RFSP) to 3.9% of GDP, a real improvement, but still above the 2.5% the IMF recommends, and that this effort is not enough to stabilize debt. The think tank warns that meeting the targets depends on record tax collection, a sharp cut in support for Pemex, and tight spending, with any shortfall likely falling on investment, health and education.

key_number.what: Projected broad public deficit (RFSP) as a share of GDP in 2027 if the Economic Package is approved, 1.9 points below 2024

items.name: IMEF (Instituto Mexicano de Ejecutivos de Finanzas)
items.title: Información estratégica para líderes financieros: nuevo reporte IMEF
items.summary: The IMEF says Mexico's public finances are under pressure, with a broad public-sector deficit of 4.8% at the end of 2025, well above the 3.9% the government initially planned. It warns that high debt, continued support for Pemex and new labour costs bring Mexico closer to losing its investment-grade rating, and it expects weak growth of 1.3% in 2026.

key_number.what: The broad public-sector fiscal deficit (RFSP) at the close of 2025, well above the 3.9% initially planned by the government.
